copy.aboutLead: A developer with a background in live sound engineering and studio production, now building interactive systems and game architecture in in Unity, C#, and FMOD
copy.aboutParagraph1: I'm a developer with a background in live sound engineering and studio production, currently transitioning into game development — building interactive systems and game architecture in Unity/C#.
copy.aboutParagraph2: My professional foundation comes from front-of-house mixing, concert productions, and studio work, where I built a practical understanding of signal flow, DSP, and acoustic behavior. I'm now applying that background toward game development, focused on learning how to build clean, extensible system architectures in Unity/C#.
copy.focusAreas: Unity & C#, Gameplay systems, Responsive controls, Game feel, FMOD, Audio implementation, Sound design
copy.principlesText: Every interaction has a rhythm. I like making that rhythm feel clear, playful and satisfying — through code, sound, or the way they work together.

copy.aboutParagraph3: In parallel, I continue exploring the intersection of audio and code — procedural acoustics, adaptive music systems, and game audio middleware like FMOD. Over time, I want these two paths — systems programming and audio engineering — to converge into a single, coherent skill set rather than stay separate.
